Contract for Buying a Horse Checklist

A horse purchase contract checklist is a detailed inventory of essential terms, clauses, and contingencies that buyers and sellers should include in a written agreement when transferring ownership of an equine to protect both parties and prevent misunderstandings.

Published 14 November 2026 · Wise Covington PLLC

Why You Need a Written Horse Sale Agreement

Buying or selling an equine involves significant financial investment and liability. Many transactions happen on a handshake, which often leads to disputes when unexpected health issues or behavioral problems arise after the sale. A clear, written contract sets expectations and provides a roadmap if something goes wrong. Relying on oral promises makes it very difficult to prove what was agreed upon if a disagreement reaches court.

When drafting or reviewing your agreement, you might wonder about templates. To learn more about this approach, read Can I Use a Template I Found Online for a Horse Legal Guide. You may also want to explore Do I Need a Contract to Buy a Horse? Horse Legal Guide to understand the broader legal context of equine transactions. Every horse sale is unique, and standard online forms rarely cover the specific details of your situation.

  • Identifies the exact buyer and seller involved
  • Establishes the precise purchase price and payment terms
  • Outlines who bears the risk of loss during transport
  • Reduces the likelihood of costly post-sale litigation

Identifying Information and Purchase Price Details

The foundation of any solid horse purchase agreement is accurate identification. The contract must describe the animal in detail, including registered name, registration number, breed, color, sex, age, and any distinctive markings or microchip numbers. Vague descriptions can create severe problems if a dispute arises over which animal was actually sold and transferred.

Next, the contract must clearly state the total purchase price, the currency, and the precise payment schedule. If the transaction involves installment payments, deposits, or contingencies based on future events, every detail must be recorded in writing. You can find more structured payment guidance in the resource titled Horse Sale Contract with Payments Horse Legal Guide. Clear payment terms protect the seller from non-payment and give the buyer certainty regarding their financial obligations.

  • Full registered and barn name of the equine
  • Microchip number, tattoo, or distinct markings
  • Total purchase price and currency type
  • Exact dates and amounts for any installment payments

Pre-Purchase Exams and Health Warranties

Health and soundness are frequently the most contentious subjects in equine sales. A proper contract checklist should always address whether a pre-purchase veterinary examination is required, who selects and pays for the veterinarian, and what specific findings might allow the buyer to cancel the contract and receive a refund.

Sellers often provide limited warranties regarding the current health of the animal, while buyers often seek broader guarantees. State law generally governs whether a horse is considered a good or livestock under the Uniform Commercial Code, which can heavily impact implied warranties of merchantability or fitness. Because these rules vary significantly across jurisdictions, you must examine the specific statutes and case law in your state to understand how warranties apply to livestock transactions.

  • Contingency clause for pre-purchase veterinary exam results
  • Explicit statement of as-is sale versus health warranties
  • Disclosure of known vices, past injuries, or chronic medical conditions
  • Timeline for the buyer to inspect and accept the animal

Registration Papers, Risk of Loss, and Governing Law

Transferring ownership requires managing administrative details alongside the physical animal. The contract should state precisely when registration papers, Coggins test results, and signed transfer applications will be handed over to the buyer. Delays in receiving breed association paperwork can hinder the new owner from showing or breeding the animal as planned.

Additionally, the agreement must specify when the risk of loss transfers from the seller to the buyer. Does the risk shift when the contract is signed, when payment clears, or when the horse steps onto the trailer? Finally, the contract should name the state law that governs the agreement and the specific county where any legal disputes must be resolved, giving both parties predictability if a disagreement occurs.

  • Timeline for delivering breed registration transfer papers
  • Clear assignment of risk of loss during transit
  • Designation of governing state law and venue for disputes
  • Signatures and dates for both buyer and authorized seller

What the sources say

  • The Uniform Commercial Code governs the sale of goods, including livestock like horses, in almost all United States jurisdictions. (Cornell Law School Legal Information Institute)
  • State statutes of frauds typically require contracts for the sale of goods above a certain monetary threshold to be in writing to be enforceable. (Wikipedia)

Frequently asked questions

What happens if a horse gets sick before delivery?

This depends heavily on how your contract allocates the risk of loss and whether a transport contingency was included in the written agreement. State law generally looks to the terms of the contract to determine which party bears the financial burden if the animal is injured or falls ill before reaching the buyer.

Are verbal agreements legally binding for horse sales?

Verbal agreements can sometimes be legally binding, but they are extremely difficult to enforce because proving what was said is often impossible. Many states enforce the Statute of Frauds for higher-value sales, which requires certain contracts to be in writing to be legally enforceable in court.

Should a pre-purchase exam be mentioned in the contract?

Yes, including the pre-purchase exam in the contract ensures both parties agree on the inspection timeline, the veterinarian involved, and whether failing specific veterinary checks allows the buyer to cancel the transaction and recover their deposit without penalty or dispute.

Does state law affect horse sale contracts?

Yes, state law heavily impacts horse sale contracts because livestock transactions are often governed by state commercial codes, specific equine activity statutes, and local laws regarding consumer protection, warranties, and the statute of frauds for high-value sales.
